A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiNeS research. All 31 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, support comparison. Retained equations, tables, and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 and the appendices report original LiNeS experiments on forgetting, vision/NLP model merging, distribution shifts, and LLM reward-policy merging.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional sensitivity, ConvNeXt, regularized fine-tuning, and LoRA experiments in Appendices C.6–C.9.

M1.justification: The depth-dependent linear residual scaling, intercept heuristic, merging procedures, and decoder-only application to T5 remain unchanged. The ConvNeXt and LoRA experiments evaluate the existing method without introducing a new LiNeS component.

E1.justification: The vision and NLP benchmarks, ImageNet distribution shifts, and Reddit summarization task are retained. Added appendix experiments reuse existing vision tasks while varying architecture, fine-tuning procedure, or hyperparameters; they do not introduce new data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix C.8 and Table 10 add four evaluated alternatives: linear and exponential layer-wise learning-rate schedules, freezing the first half of the blocks, and training only the final block. These substantially extend comparison to training-time approaches for preserving generalization. Existing merging comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include one- and two-dimensional hyperparameter sweeps, ConvNeXt evaluations, four regularized fine-tuning configurations, and ViT-B/32 LoRA experiments at ranks 16, 32, 64, and 128 with LoRA alpha equal to rank. These extend experimental settings without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds sensitivity curves and a joint alpha–beta grid examining robustness and the intercept heuristic. Appendices C.7 and C.9 test forgetting under convolutional architectures and varying LoRA ranks. Earlier scaling-function, target/control weighting, and T5 encoder/decoder analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The additions introduce no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Reporting continues through task-averaged results and performance curves; the statistical reporting of retained experiments is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the original plotted results are retained. Substantial new results appear in Figures 8–10 and Tables 8–11. For example, new Table 9 reports ConvNeXt Task Arithmetic accuracy of 77.9 without LiNeS and 79.0 with it. Table 11 reports rank-128 LoRA control accuracy of 41.6 versus 46.3, with target accuracy of 87.5 versus 87.2.

T1.justification: Appendix C.9 adds a mathematical specification of LoRA's weight update and low-rank condition, although the printed factor dimensions are inconsistent with the BA product. The LiNeS equations and intercept heuristic remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract foregrounds forgetting and merging interference as two challenges, but retains the same scientific contribution. Claims about preserving generalization, improving model merging and OOD performance, and applicability to reward-aligned LLM policies remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The new sensitivity discussion interprets the grid-search optima as supporting the intercept heuristic and positive layer-increasing scaling. The LoRA discussion relates increased expressivity to the target-performance/forgetting trade-off. Existing qualifications about T5 encoder scaling and improved control performance after NLP fine-tuning are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 newly discloses LLaMA LoRA rank 64, scaling alpha 128, and dropout 0.05, without establishing that the experiment changed. Table 8 supplies selected LiNeS coefficients, and the new appendices describe regularization and LoRA settings. The existing code link is relocated without changing the referenced resource.

R1.justification: New citations include LoRA, ConvNeXt, layer-wise linear mode connectivity, Model Stock, Pareto low-rank adapters, and task addition in closed-vocabulary models. The Raghu work on rapid learning versus feature reuse is removed. The overall positioning remains stable; numerous other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract is reframed, Section 3 gains a summary of the new studies, and Appendix C gains four subsections. The main section order and most prose remain intact. Author/header text and local wording change; Appendix A also acquires a garbled docstring sentence.

P2.justification: The appendix gains sensitivity curves, annotated two-dimensional heatmaps, a ConvNeXt scatter plot, and tables presenting configurations and new comparisons. These substantially expand the visual evidence. Original figures are retained, sometimes relocated or renumbered, while the pseudocode is reformatted with syntax highlighting.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important validation gaps in v1: Figures 8–9 directly examine the fixed-intercept heuristic, and Table 10 compares LiNeS with relevant training-time alternatives for preserving shallow-layer features. ConvNeXt and LoRA experiments further test applicability beyond the original configurations. These targeted additions substantially strengthen the empirical justification for the method. Localized notation and docstring errors do not outweigh those gains.
